pharmaceuticals.name: Short-acting β2 agonist (SABA)
pharmaceuticals.use: Rescue relief of acute bronchospasm; the reliever, not the controller.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Rising reliever use is the clearest sign asthma control is failing — escalate the controller, do not just refill.

pharmaceuticals.name: Long-acting β2 agonist (LABA)
pharmaceuticals.use: Maintenance bronchodilation in asthma and COPD.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Never as monotherapy in asthma — always paired with an inhaled corticosteroid.

pharmaceuticals.name: Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA)
pharmaceuticals.use: First-line maintenance in COPD; add-on in severe asthma.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Caution in narrow-angle glaucoma and bladder outlet obstruction.

pharmaceuticals.name: Short-acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA)
pharmaceuticals.use: Acute bronchospasm, often combined with a SABA in exacerbations.

pharmaceuticals.name: Inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)
pharmaceuticals.use: Long-term control of persistent asthma — recommended for every patient with persistent asthma.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Rinse and spit to prevent oral candidiasis and dysphonia. In COPD reserved for frequent exacerbators or an eosinophilic phenotype — it raises pneumonia risk.

pharmaceuticals.name: ICS/LABA combination inhaler
pharmaceuticals.use: Maintenance, and in asthma also reliever therapy where a formoterol combination is used.

pharmaceuticals.name: Leukotriene receptor antagonist
pharmaceuticals.use: Add-on in asthma, especially with allergic rhinitis or exercise-induced symptoms.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Boxed warning for serious neuropsychiatric events — ask directly about mood, sleep and suicidal thoughts.

pharmaceuticals.name: PDE4 inhibitor
pharmaceuticals.use: Severe COPD with chronic bronchitis and repeated exacerbations.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Weight loss, diarrhoea and psychiatric effects are common reasons for stopping.

pharmaceuticals.name: Methylxanthine
pharmaceuticals.use: Third-line bronchodilation where inhaled therapy is not enough.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Narrow therapeutic index — levels needed; many interactions.

pharmaceuticals.name: Systemic corticosteroid
pharmaceuticals.use: Short bursts for asthma and COPD exacerbations, and for sarcoidosis and autoimmune flares.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Hyperglycaemia, bone loss, adrenal suppression and mood change with repeated or prolonged courses.

pharmaceuticals.name: Respiratory biologics
pharmaceuticals.use: Severe asthma not controlled on inhaled therapy, targeted by phenotype.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Specialist-initiated; phenotype (IgE, eosinophils) decides the agent.

pharmaceuticals.name: Antifibrotics
pharmaceuticals.use: Slowing decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: LFT monitoring; photosensitivity with pirfenidone, diarrhoea with nintedanib.

pharmaceuticals.name: Varenicline
pharmaceuticals.use: Partial nicotine receptor agonist for smoking cessation — the single highest-yield intervention in COPD.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Active suicidal ideation is a contraindication. Screen mood before prescribing and at follow-up.

pharmaceuticals.name: Nicotine replacement therapy
pharmaceuticals.use: Patch for background craving with a short-acting form for breakthrough.

pharmaceuticals.name: Bupropion
pharmaceuticals.use: Smoking cessation, and depression where sexual side effects or sedation are unwanted.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Lowers the seizure threshold — avoid in seizure disorder, bulimia and anorexia. Can worsen anxiety.

pharmaceuticals.name: Mucolytics and expectorants
pharmaceuticals.use: Loosening tenacious secretions.
pharmaceuticals.examples: guaifenesin, hypertonic saline, dornase alfa (cystic fibrosis)

pharmaceuticals.name: Respiratory antibiotics
pharmaceuticals.use: Bacterial pneumonia, bacterial sinusitis, and COPD exacerbations with purulent sputum.
pharmaceuticals.examples: amoxicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, doxycycline, azithromycin, respiratory fluoroquinolones
pharmaceuticals.caution: Not for uncomplicated viral URI or acute bronchitis — both are clinical diagnoses and usually viral.

pharmaceuticals.name: Neuraminidase inhibitor
pharmaceuticals.use: Influenza, best within 48 hours of onset; consider in high-risk groups.

pharmaceuticals.name: COVID-19 antivirals
pharmaceuticals.use: Early treatment in patients at risk of progression.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir has extensive CYP3A4 interactions — screen the whole medication and supplement list.

pharmaceuticals.name: Second-generation antihistamine
pharmaceuticals.use: Allergic rhinitis, urticaria and the histamine component of atopy.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Far less sedating than first-generation agents; preferred for daytime use.

pharmaceuticals.name: First-generation antihistamine
pharmaceuticals.use: Short-term itch and sleep where sedation is acceptable.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Anticholinergic — avoid in older adults, and with glaucoma or urinary retention.

pharmaceuticals.name: Intranasal corticosteroid
pharmaceuticals.use: First-line for persistent allergic rhinitis and an adjunct in sinusitis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Aim away from the septum to avoid epistaxis; takes days to work.

pharmaceuticals.name: Decongestants
pharmaceuticals.use: Short-term relief of nasal congestion.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Topical agents cause rebound congestion beyond 3 days; oral agents raise blood pressure.

pharmaceuticals.name: Compounded antifungal nasal spray
pharmaceuticals.use: Fungal sinus colonisation in mould-exposed and treatment-resistant patients.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Compounded; from your mould lecture — well tolerated, including in children.

pharmaceuticals.name: SSRI
pharmaceuticals.use: First-line drug therapy in depression, GAD, panic, OCD and PTSD.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Serotonin syndrome risk with St John's wort, tramadol, triptans, MAOIs and methylene blue. Activation and suicidality warning in under-25s; taper on stopping.

pharmaceuticals.name: SNRI
pharmaceuticals.use: Depression and GAD, and useful where neuropathic pain or fibromyalgia coexist.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Dose-dependent blood pressure rise with venlafaxine; marked discontinuation syndrome.

pharmaceuticals.name: Mirtazapine
pharmaceuticals.use: Depression with insomnia and poor appetite or weight loss.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Sedation and appetite gain are strongest at low doses.

pharmaceuticals.name: Trazodone
pharmaceuticals.use: Low dose for sleep onset; higher doses for depression.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Orthostatic hypotension; priapism is rare but urgent.

pharmaceuticals.name: Tricyclic antidepressant
pharmaceuticals.use: Migraine prophylaxis, neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia; less used now for depression.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Anticholinergic and cardiotoxic in overdose — caution where suicide risk is present.

pharmaceuticals.name: Buspirone
pharmaceuticals.use: Generalised anxiety without the dependence risk of benzodiazepines.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Slow onset — weeks, not hours.

pharmaceuticals.name: Benzodiazepine
pharmaceuticals.use: Short-term crisis anxiety and panic; alcohol withdrawal.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Not recommended in PTSD — they interfere with extinction learning, the goal of trauma therapy, and carry a high dependence risk. Additive with alcohol and opioids.

pharmaceuticals.name: Non-benzodiazepine hypnotic
pharmaceuticals.use: Short-term insomnia.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Complex sleep behaviours carry a boxed warning; tolerance builds quickly.

pharmaceuticals.name: Lithium carbonate
pharmaceuticals.use: Bipolar disorder — the strongest anti-suicide evidence of any psychotropic.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Narrow therapeutic index. Levels, renal and thyroid function needed. NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and thiazides raise levels; dehydration is dangerous.

pharmaceuticals.name: Anticonvulsant mood stabilisers
pharmaceuticals.use: Bipolar maintenance and mania; lamotrigine favours the depressed pole.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Lamotrigine needs slow titration for Stevens-Johnson risk. Valproate and carbamazepine are teratogenic; carbamazepine is a strong enzyme inducer.

pharmaceuticals.name: Second-generation antipsychotic
pharmaceuticals.use: Acute mania, bipolar depression, and augmentation in resistant depression.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Metabolic syndrome, weight gain and QT prolongation — monitor weight, glucose and lipids.

pharmaceuticals.name: Ketamine / esketamine
pharmaceuticals.use: Treatment-resistant depression and suicidality; rapid onset, given as IV infusion or intranasal esketamine.
pharmaceuticals.caution: NMDA receptor antagonist that rapidly raises BDNF and promotes synaptogenesis. Dissociation and blood pressure rise require monitored administration.

pharmaceuticals.name: Prazosin
pharmaceuticals.use: PTSD-related nightmares and sleep disturbance.
pharmaceuticals.caution: First-dose orthostatic hypotension — start low, at night.

pharmaceuticals.name: Methylene blue
pharmaceuticals.use: Studied as an adjunct to exposure therapy — enhances mitochondrial electron transport and helps consolidate fear-extinction memories.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Has MAOI properties. Avoid or use with extreme caution alongside SSRIs, SNRIs or any serotonergic agent — serotonin syndrome risk.

pharmaceuticals.name: Low-dose naltrexone
pharmaceuticals.use: Off-label for fibromyalgia, chronic pain, sarcoidosis and autoimmune conditions.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Blocks opioid analgesia; stop before procedures needing opioids.

pharmaceuticals.name: Proton pump inhibitor
pharmaceuticals.use: GERD, erosive oesophagitis, peptic ulcer, H. pylori regimens.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Aim for the shortest effective course. Long-term use is linked to B12, magnesium and iron malabsorption, C. difficile and fracture risk; rebound acid on abrupt stopping — taper.

pharmaceuticals.name: H2 receptor antagonist
pharmaceuticals.use: Milder or intermittent reflux, and night-time breakthrough on a PPI.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Tolerance develops within weeks.

pharmaceuticals.name: Antacids and alginates
pharmaceuticals.use: On-demand symptomatic relief; alginate rafts suit postprandial and night reflux.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Separate from other medicines by two hours — they impair absorption.

pharmaceuticals.name: Sucralfate
pharmaceuticals.use: Ulcer and mucosal protection; coats the ulcer base.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Binds other drugs — dose apart.

pharmaceuticals.name: Prokinetics
pharmaceuticals.use: Gastroparesis and refractory reflux with delayed emptying.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Metoclopramide carries a tardive dyskinesia boxed warning — limit to 12 weeks.

pharmaceuticals.name: Antispasmodics
pharmaceuticals.use: Cramping pain in irritable bowel syndrome.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Anticholinergic burden; avoid in older adults.

pharmaceuticals.name: Rifaximin
pharmaceuticals.use: IBS with diarrhoea and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Poorly absorbed, so systemic effects are few; relapse is common.

pharmaceuticals.name: Loperamide
pharmaceuticals.use: Symptomatic control of non-infectious diarrhoea.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Avoid where there is fever or bloody stool — it prolongs invasive infection. QT prolongation at high doses.

pharmaceuticals.name: Laxatives
pharmaceuticals.use: Constipation — osmotic agents first, stimulants for rescue.
pharmaceuticals.examples: polyethylene glycol, lactulose, magnesium, senna, docusate
pharmaceuticals.caution: Stimulant laxatives are for short-term use. Correct fibre, fluid and thyroid status first.

pharmaceuticals.name: Ondansetron
pharmaceuticals.use: Nausea and vomiting.
pharmaceuticals.caution: QT prolongation; constipation.

pharmaceuticals.name: 5-aminosalicylates
pharmaceuticals.use: Inflammatory bowel disease, mainly ulcerative colitis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Monitor renal function.

pharmaceuticals.name: Ursodeoxycholic acid
pharmaceuticals.use: Dissolving small cholesterol gallstones and in cholestatic liver disease.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Only works on small, non-calcified stones and takes months; recurrence is common.

pharmaceuticals.name: H. pylori eradication regimen
pharmaceuticals.use: Confirmed H. pylori gastritis or ulcer.
pharmaceuticals.examples: PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin, or bismuth quadruple therapy
pharmaceuticals.caution: Test-of-cure at least 4 weeks after finishing, off PPI.

pharmaceuticals.name: Antiparasitics
pharmaceuticals.use: Confirmed intestinal parasites, chosen by organism.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Treat on a positive stool test, not on suspicion alone.

pharmaceuticals.name: Statin
pharmaceuticals.use: Cardiovascular risk reduction in atherosclerosis and diabetes.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Myalgia is common and usually reversible; check CK if severe. Interacts with grapefruit and red yeast rice — never combine the two.

pharmaceuticals.name: ACE inhibitor
pharmaceuticals.use: Hypertension, heart failure, and renal protection in diabetic kidney disease.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Dry cough (up to 20%) and angio-oedema. Contraindicated in pregnancy. Check potassium and creatinine after starting.

pharmaceuticals.name: Angiotensin receptor blocker
pharmaceuticals.use: As for ACE inhibitors, and the usual substitute when cough intervenes.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Contraindicated in pregnancy; same potassium and renal monitoring.

pharmaceuticals.name: Calcium channel blocker
pharmaceuticals.use: Hypertension, and dihydropyridines for Raynaud's and vasospasm.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Ankle oedema and constipation. Non-dihydropyridines are negatively inotropic — avoid in reduced ejection fraction.

pharmaceuticals.name: Thiazide diuretic
pharmaceuticals.use: First-line hypertension; reduces calcium excretion in stone formers.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia, raised urate and glucose. Raises lithium levels.

pharmaceuticals.name: Beta blocker
pharmaceuticals.use: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, post-infarct, rate control, migraine prophylaxis, performance anxiety.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Caution in asthma and in Raynaud's, where they worsen vasospasm.

pharmaceuticals.name: Loop diuretic
pharmaceuticals.use: Fluid overload in heart failure, and oedema from renal or hepatic causes.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Electrolyte loss, dehydration, ototoxicity at high doses. Daily weights guide the dose.

pharmaceuticals.name: Mineralocorticoid antagonist
pharmaceuticals.use: Heart failure, resistant hypertension; and the androgenic features of PCOS and acne.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Hyperkalaemia — monitor potassium, and avoid combining with potassium supplements or ACE inhibitors without checking.

pharmaceuticals.name: Nitrates
pharmaceuticals.use: Angina relief and prophylaxis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Absolutely contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors — profound hypotension.

pharmaceuticals.name: Low-dose aspirin
pharmaceuticals.use: Secondary prevention after a cardiovascular event.
pharmaceuticals.caution: GI bleeding risk. Avoid in children and teenagers with a viral illness — Reye's syndrome.

pharmaceuticals.name: Anticoagulants
pharmaceuticals.use: Atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, pulmonary embolism.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Bleeding risk. Warfarin interacts with vitamin K, many herbs and foods; DOACs have fewer but real interactions. Never start a supplement affecting platelets without checking.

pharmaceuticals.name: Metformin
pharmaceuticals.use: First-line in type 2 diabetes; also used in PCOS for insulin resistance.
pharmaceuticals.caution: GI upset; B12 depletion over years — check it. Hold around contrast imaging and in acute illness.

pharmaceuticals.name: GLP-1 receptor agonist
pharmaceuticals.use: Type 2 diabetes with obesity; substantial weight loss.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Nausea, delayed gastric emptying; pancreatitis and thyroid C-cell warnings.

pharmaceuticals.name: SGLT2 inhibitor
pharmaceuticals.use: Type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular or renal disease; heart failure independent of diabetes.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Genital mycotic infection, volume depletion, and euglycaemic ketoacidosis.

pharmaceuticals.name: Sulfonylureas
pharmaceuticals.use: Type 2 diabetes where cost governs.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Hypoglycaemia and weight gain.

pharmaceuticals.name: Insulin
pharmaceuticals.use: Type 1 diabetes and advanced type 2.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Hypoglycaemia; needs structured education and monitoring.

pharmaceuticals.name: Levothyroxine
pharmaceuticals.use: Hypothyroidism.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Take fasted, and separate by four hours from calcium, iron, magnesium and coffee. Recheck TSH 6–8 weeks after any change.

pharmaceuticals.name: Antithyroid drugs
pharmaceuticals.use: Hyperthyroidism and Graves' disease.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Agranulocytosis — any sore throat or fever needs an urgent white cell count. Propylthiouracil is preferred in the first trimester.

pharmaceuticals.name: NSAIDs
pharmaceuticals.use: Inflammatory and nociceptive pain, gout flares, dysmenorrhoea.
pharmaceuticals.caution: GI bleeding, renal impairment, blood pressure rise, and raised lithium levels. Avoid in chronic kidney disease and heart failure.

pharmaceuticals.name: Acetaminophen / paracetamol
pharmaceuticals.use: First-line simple analgesia, including where NSAIDs are unsafe.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Hepatotoxic in overdose and at lower doses with alcohol or fasting; count every combination product.

pharmaceuticals.name: Colchicine
pharmaceuticals.use: Acute gout, and prophylaxis when starting urate-lowering therapy.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Diarrhoea is dose-limiting; reduce in renal impairment; interacts with statins and CYP3A4 inhibitors.

pharmaceuticals.name: Urate-lowering therapy
pharmaceuticals.use: Recurrent gout, tophi, or urate stones.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Can precipitate a flare when started — cover with prophylaxis. Allopurinol hypersensitivity is rare but severe.

pharmaceuticals.name: Conventional DMARDs
pharmaceuticals.use: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic disease, sarcoidosis, and other autoimmune conditions.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Methotrexate needs weekly dosing with folate, and CBC and LFT monitoring; it is teratogenic. Hydroxychloroquine needs annual retinal screening.

pharmaceuticals.name: Immunologic biologics
pharmaceuticals.use: Moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease.
pharmaceuticals.examples: TNF inhibitors, IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors, rituximab
pharmaceuticals.caution: Screen for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B before starting; infection risk throughout.

pharmaceuticals.name: Gabapentinoids
pharmaceuticals.use: Neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, restless legs.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Sedation, dizziness, oedema; dose-reduce in renal impairment; misuse potential.

pharmaceuticals.name: Muscle relaxants
pharmaceuticals.use: Short courses for acute muscle spasm in neck and back pain.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Sedation and anticholinergic effects; not for long-term use.

pharmaceuticals.name: Triptans
pharmaceuticals.use: Acute migraine, taken early in the attack.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension and coronary disease; serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs. Limit to under 10 days a month to avoid medication-overuse headache.

pharmaceuticals.name: CGRP-targeted therapies
pharmaceuticals.use: Migraine prevention, and gepants for acute treatment.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Constipation with some agents; specialist-initiated.

pharmaceuticals.name: Topiramate
pharmaceuticals.use: Migraine prophylaxis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Cognitive slowing, paraesthesia, kidney stones, weight loss; teratogenic.

pharmaceuticals.name: Bisphosphonates
pharmaceuticals.use: Osteoporosis and fracture prevention.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Take upright, fasted, with water. Correct vitamin D and calcium first. Rare osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fracture.

pharmaceuticals.name: Denosumab
pharmaceuticals.use: Osteoporosis where bisphosphonates are unsuitable or renal function is poor.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Rebound vertebral fracture on stopping — never discontinue without a follow-on agent.

pharmaceuticals.name: Alpha-1 blocker
pharmaceuticals.use: Benign prostatic hyperplasia — fastest symptom relief.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Orthostatic hypotension and retrograde ejaculation; tell the ophthalmologist before cataract surgery.

pharmaceuticals.name: 5-alpha reductase inhibitor
pharmaceuticals.use: Larger prostates — shrinks the gland over months.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Halves the PSA — double the measured value when interpreting. Sexual side effects may persist.

pharmaceuticals.name: Overactive bladder agents
pharmaceuticals.use: Urgency incontinence after pelvic floor training.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Anticholinergics add to cognitive burden in older adults; mirabegron raises blood pressure.

pharmaceuticals.name: Urinary antibiotics
pharmaceuticals.use: Uncomplicated cystitis and pyelonephritis, guided by local resistance.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Nitrofurantoin does not treat pyelonephritis and needs adequate renal function. Fluoroquinolones carry tendon and neuropathy warnings.

pharmaceuticals.name: Prostate-penetrating antibiotics
pharmaceuticals.use: Bacterial prostatitis — long courses are needed to penetrate the gland.
pharmaceuticals.caution: 4–6 weeks in chronic disease.

pharmaceuticals.name: Combined oral contraceptive
pharmaceuticals.use: Cycle control in PCOS, dysmenorrhoea, endometriosis and acne.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Thrombosis risk, raised in smokers over 35 and with migraine with aura. St John's wort reduces effectiveness.

pharmaceuticals.name: Progestins and hormonal IUD
pharmaceuticals.use: Endometriosis, heavy menstrual bleeding, endometrial protection.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Irregular bleeding early on.

pharmaceuticals.name: Menopausal hormone therapy
pharmaceuticals.use: Vasomotor symptoms, and vaginal oestrogen for genitourinary syndrome of menopause.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Systemic therapy needs an individual risk discussion; unopposed oestrogen is unsafe with a uterus. Vaginal oestrogen is minimally absorbed.

pharmaceuticals.name: Ovulation induction
pharmaceuticals.use: Anovulatory infertility, mainly in PCOS — letrozole is first-line.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Multiple pregnancy risk; needs monitoring.

pharmaceuticals.name: GnRH agonists and antagonists
pharmaceuticals.use: Endometriosis pain unresponsive to first-line therapy.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Induces a hypo-oestrogenic state — bone loss; add-back therapy is usual.

pharmaceuticals.name: Tranexamic acid
pharmaceuticals.use: Heavy menstrual bleeding, taken only on bleeding days.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Avoid with a thrombosis history.

pharmaceuticals.name: Topical corticosteroid
pharmaceuticals.use: Eczema and psoriasis flares, matched in potency to the site.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Skin atrophy with prolonged use; use the lowest effective potency on the face and flexures.

pharmaceuticals.name: Topical calcineurin inhibitors
pharmaceuticals.use: Eczema on the face, eyelids and flexures, sparing steroids.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Transient burning on application.

pharmaceuticals.name: Topical retinoid
pharmaceuticals.use: Acne — the core of any comedonal regimen.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Irritation and photosensitivity; contraindicated in pregnancy.

pharmaceuticals.name: Benzoyl peroxide
pharmaceuticals.use: Acne, and pairing it with any topical antibiotic limits resistance.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Bleaches fabric; drying.

pharmaceuticals.name: Acne antibiotics
pharmaceuticals.use: Inflammatory acne, always alongside benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid, not alone.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Doxycycline causes photosensitivity and oesophagitis — take upright with water.

pharmaceuticals.name: Isotretinoin
pharmaceuticals.use: Severe nodulocystic or scarring acne.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy — pregnancy prevention programme required. LFT and lipid monitoring; mood change.

pharmaceuticals.name: Antifungals
pharmaceuticals.use: Candidiasis, tinea and onychomycosis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Azoles inhibit CYP3A4 — check interactions. Terbinafine and oral azoles need LFT awareness.

pharmaceuticals.name: Herpes antivirals
pharmaceuticals.use: Herpes simplex and zoster — episodic or suppressive.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Start within 72 hours; adjust for renal function.

pharmaceuticals.name: Topical ocular antibiotics
pharmaceuticals.use: Bacterial conjunctivitis.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Most conjunctivitis is viral and self-limiting; a contact-lens wearer needs urgent review.

pharmaceuticals.name: Hepatitis antivirals
pharmaceuticals.use: Chronic hepatitis B and C, chosen by genotype and stage.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Specialist-directed; direct-acting antivirals cure most hepatitis C. Screen before immunosuppression.

pharmaceuticals.name: Hydroxyzine
pharmaceuticals.use: Short-term anxiety and itch without dependence risk.
pharmaceuticals.caution: Sedating and anticholinergic; QT prolongation at high doses.

supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA)
supplements.mech: Anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective; lowers triglycerides. Your mental health notes give 1–3 g for depression, bipolar and PTSD.
supplements.caution: Additive with anticoagulants and antiplatelets at higher doses. Choose a tested product for oxidation and heavy metals.

supplements.name: Magnesium glycinate
supplements.mech: Calming; cofactor in over 300 reactions. Your notes name the glycinate form specifically for absorption and neurological support.
supplements.caution: Citrate and oxide forms are more laxative. Reduce in renal impairment.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.mech: Immune modulation, bone health, mood. Deficiency is itself associated with sleep apnoea severity.
supplements.caution: Test rather than guess; take with fat and with vitamin K2 when dosing high.

supplements.name: B-complex (B6, B9, B12)
supplements.mech: Cofactors for neurotransmitter synthesis and methylation. B6 as P5P is the cofactor for GABA synthesis.
supplements.caution: High-dose B6 over long periods causes peripheral neuropathy. Check B12 before folate to avoid masking deficiency.

supplements.name: Lithium orotate
supplements.mech: Low-dose lithium for mood and anxiety; crosses the blood-brain barrier more readily than the carbonate form.
supplements.caution: Not a substitute for prescription lithium in bipolar I. Your notes give the 5–20 mg range.

supplements.name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
supplements.mech: 5-HT1A agonism, FAAH inhibition raising anandamide, and reduced amygdala reactivity — the three mechanisms in your notes.
supplements.caution: Inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 — check interactions. Legal status varies.

supplements.name: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera)
supplements.mech: Adaptogen; modulates the HPA axis and lowers cortisol.
supplements.caution: Avoid in hyperthyroidism — it raises thyroid hormones. Rare hepatotoxicity. Nightshade family.

supplements.name: Saffron (Crocus sativus)
supplements.mech: Raises serotonin; trials show efficacy comparable to fluoxetine in mild to moderate depression. Your notes give 30 mg.
supplements.caution: Additive with serotonergic drugs.

supplements.name: L-theanine
supplements.mech: Promotes alpha brain waves and enhances GABA — anxiolytic without sedation.
supplements.caution: Well tolerated; may lower blood pressure.

supplements.name: Lavender (Silexan)
supplements.mech: Modulates GABA receptors; trial evidence in anxiety comparable to low-dose anxiolytics.
supplements.caution: Eructation with a lavender taste.

supplements.name: Chamomile (Matricaria)
supplements.mech: Mild sedative; apigenin binds benzodiazepine receptors.
supplements.caution: Asteraceae allergy.

supplements.name: SAMe
supplements.mech: Methyl donor used in depression and osteoarthritis.
supplements.caution: AVOID IN BIPOLAR — can induce mania or hypomania through serotonergic and methylation effects. Serotonergic interactions.

supplements.name: St John's wort (Hypericum)
supplements.mech: Mild to moderate depression.
supplements.caution: AVOID IN BIPOLAR — documented to trigger mania and cycling. A potent CYP3A4 inducer: do not combine with SSRIs (serotonin syndrome), oral contraceptives, or anticoagulants.

supplements.name: Rhodiola rosea
supplements.mech: Stimulating adaptogen for fatigue and stress resilience.
supplements.caution: AVOID IN BIPOLAR — as a stimulating adaptogen it may worsen agitation or induce hypomania. Can disturb sleep if taken late.

supplements.name: Panax ginseng
supplements.mech: Stimulating adaptogen for fatigue and cognition.
supplements.caution: Caution in bipolar disorder — stimulating botanicals risk mood destabilisation. Raises blood pressure in some.

supplements.name: N-acetyl cysteine (NAC)
supplements.mech: Mucolytic and glutathione precursor. Named in your respiratory quizzes as the mucolytic of choice in COPD, and in the mould lecture as the gentler glutathione alternative in sensitive patients.
supplements.caution: Nausea at higher doses. In active mould exposure your notes prefer NAC over glutathione, which can mobilise toxins.

supplements.name: Quercetin
supplements.mech: Mast-cell stabiliser and antihistamine-like flavonoid; anti-inflammatory in allergy and asthma.
supplements.caution: Take with bromelain or as phytosome for absorption; inhibits CYP3A4.

supplements.name: Resveratrol
supplements.mech: Anti-inflammatory and antithrombotic — your COVID quiz names it as the agent addressing both inflammation and thrombus formation.
supplements.caution: Mild antiplatelet effect; caution with anticoagulants.

supplements.name: Vitamin C
supplements.mech: Antioxidant; supports immune function and collagen synthesis; shortens cold duration modestly.
supplements.caution: Loose stool at bowel tolerance. Caution with a history of oxalate stones.

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.mech: Immune function, wound healing, taste and smell; lozenges shorten colds when started early.
supplements.caution: Take with food; over 40 mg long-term depletes copper — pair or cycle.

supplements.name: Elderberry (Sambucus nigra)
supplements.mech: Antiviral support in colds and influenza.
supplements.caution: Use cooked or standardised preparations; raw berries are emetic.

supplements.name: Bee propolis
supplements.mech: Antimicrobial and soothing in upper respiratory infection and sore throat.
supplements.caution: Avoid with bee product allergy.

supplements.name: Garlic (Allium sativum)
supplements.mech: Antimicrobial, mild antihypertensive and lipid-lowering.
supplements.caution: Antiplatelet effect — stop before surgery.

supplements.name: Boswellia serrata
supplements.mech: 5-LOX inhibitor; anti-inflammatory in arthritis, IBD and asthma.
supplements.caution: Generally well tolerated; mild GI upset.

supplements.name: Curcumin
supplements.mech: Broad anti-inflammatory acting on NF-κB.
supplements.caution: Poor absorption unless formulated. Mild antiplatelet effect; may worsen reflux in some.

supplements.name: Nattokinase
supplements.mech: Fibrinolytic enzyme used for circulation and clot burden.
supplements.caution: Additive with anticoagulants and antiplatelets — do not combine without supervision.

supplements.name: Serrapeptase
supplements.mech: Proteolytic enzyme used for mucus and fibrin.
supplements.caution: Same bleeding caution as other systemic enzymes.

supplements.name: Glutathione (liposomal or inhaled)
supplements.mech: Master antioxidant; inhaled forms studied as an asthma adjunct.
supplements.caution: Your mould lecture warns against glutathione, liver sauce and NAD+ during ACTIVE exposure — they mobilise toxins and cause redistribution. Inhaled glutathione is not safe for every asthma patient — sulphite-sensitive patients can bronchospasm.

supplements.name: PectaSol (modified citrus pectin)
supplements.dose: Start ¼ tsp, increase as tolerated
supplements.mech: The binder used in nearly all patients in your mould lecture: breaks biofilms, binds mycotoxins, lowers inflammatory cytokines.
supplements.caution: Safe during exposure and in pregnancy, and well tolerated in infants — one of the few binders your notes allow during ongoing exposure.

supplements.name: Ultra Binder
supplements.dose: Per product, away from food and medicines
supplements.mech: Broad-spectrum binder covering charcoal, clay and more.
supplements.caution: Binds nutrients and drugs — separate by at least two hours. Do not use with unmanaged constipation.

supplements.name: Saccharomyces boulardii
supplements.mech: Binds mycotoxins and helps candida; protects against antibiotic-associated and travellers' diarrhoea.
supplements.caution: Avoid in central line patients and severe immunocompromise — fungaemia risk.

supplements.name: Biocidin
supplements.dose: Titrate from a low drop count
supplements.mech: Broad botanical antimicrobial used for gut treatment; your mould lecture uses it especially in children.
supplements.caution: Start very low — die-off reactions are common.

supplements.name: Probiotics
supplements.mech: Restoring flora after antibiotics; strain-specific benefit in IBS, atopy and vaginal health.
supplements.caution: Match the strain to the indication. Caution in severe immunocompromise.

supplements.name: Lactobacillus sakei
supplements.mech: Resets the sinus microbiome after sinus treatment — the step your mould lecture puts last.

supplements.name: Iron
supplements.mech: Iron deficiency with or without anaemia.
supplements.caution: Alternate-day dosing absorbs better than daily. Take with vitamin C, away from calcium, coffee and thyroid medication. Constipation is common.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.mech: Deficiency from metformin, PPIs, gastric surgery, vegan diets, or pernicious anaemia.
supplements.caution: Check before starting folate. Methylcobalamin or hydroxocobalamin preferred.

supplements.name: Folate
supplements.mech: Methylation, red cell production, preconception neural tube protection.
supplements.caution: Never before excluding B12 deficiency — it masks the anaemia while the neuropathy progresses.

supplements.name: Iodine
supplements.mech: Thyroid hormone synthesis; deficiency is one of the nutrient gaps corrected first in your mould protocol.
supplements.caution: Excess can trigger or worsen thyroid autoimmunity — do not dose high in Hashimoto's without monitoring.

supplements.name: Selenium
supplements.mech: Cofactor for thyroid hormone conversion; lowers thyroid antibodies in Hashimoto's.
supplements.caution: Narrow window — over 400 mcg daily is toxic.

supplements.name: Calcium
supplements.dose: 500–600 mg elemental, once or twice daily
supplements.mech: Bone health where dietary intake is short.
supplements.caution: Split doses absorb better; take with vitamin D and K2. Separate from iron and thyroid medication.

supplements.name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
supplements.mech: Directs calcium to bone rather than arteries; pairs with vitamin D.
supplements.caution: Interacts with warfarin — keep intake steady and tell the prescriber.

supplements.name: Coenzyme Q10
supplements.mech: Mitochondrial support; migraine prophylaxis; replaces what statins deplete.
supplements.caution: Ubiquinol form absorbs better with age. Mild blood-pressure lowering.

supplements.name: Riboflavin (B2)
supplements.mech: Migraine prophylaxis at this specific high dose; takes 2–3 months.
supplements.caution: Turns urine bright yellow — expected.

supplements.name: Melatonin
supplements.mech: Circadian phase shifting rather than sedation; lower doses often work better than higher.
supplements.caution: Vivid dreams and morning grogginess at higher doses.

supplements.name: 5-HTP
supplements.mech: Serotonin precursor for mood and sleep.
supplements.caution: Do not combine with SSRIs, SNRIs or MAOIs — serotonin syndrome.

supplements.name: Glycine
supplements.mech: Improves sleep quality and lowers core temperature; also a phase II conjugation substrate.
supplements.caution: Well tolerated.

supplements.name: Valerian (Valeriana officinalis)
supplements.mech: Sleep onset; GABAergic.
supplements.caution: Paradoxical stimulation in a minority; additive with sedatives.

supplements.name: Passionflower (Passiflora incarnata)
supplements.mech: Anxiety and sleep; gentle GABAergic.
supplements.caution: Additive sedation.

supplements.name: Berberine
supplements.dose: 500 mg two or three times daily
supplements.mech: Lowers blood glucose and lipids comparably to metformin in trials; antimicrobial in gut dysbiosis.
supplements.caution: Inhibits CYP3A4 — many interactions. Avoid in pregnancy and in infants (kernicterus risk).

supplements.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
supplements.mech: Diabetic neuropathy and insulin sensitivity; antioxidant regenerating other antioxidants.
supplements.caution: Can lower glucose — watch with hypoglycaemic drugs. Thiamine depletion with long use.

supplements.name: Chromium picolinate
supplements.mech: Insulin sensitivity and glycaemic control.
supplements.caution: Modest effect; caution with hypoglycaemics.

supplements.name: Myo-inositol
supplements.mech: PCOS — improves ovulation, insulin sensitivity and androgen profile; also used in anxiety and OCD at higher doses.
supplements.caution: Best evidence with a 40:1 myo- to D-chiro-inositol ratio. GI upset at high doses.

supplements.name: NAD+ / nicotinamide riboside
supplements.mech: Mitochondrial and energy support.
supplements.caution: Your mould lecture says avoid NAD+ during active exposure — it mobilises toxins.

supplements.name: Deglycyrrhizinated liquorice (DGL)
supplements.mech: Mucosal healing in gastritis, ulcer and reflux without the blood-pressure effect of whole liquorice.
supplements.caution: Whole liquorice raises blood pressure and lowers potassium — DGL is the form to use long-term.

supplements.name: Slippery elm / marshmallow root
supplements.dose: As a demulcent tea or capsule
supplements.mech: Coats and soothes irritated mucosa in reflux, gastritis and IBS.
supplements.caution: Take away from medicines — it can slow absorption.

supplements.name: Enteric-coated peppermint oil
supplements.dose: 180–225 mg two or three times daily
supplements.mech: Antispasmodic with good trial evidence in IBS.
supplements.caution: Must be enteric-coated or it worsens reflux; relaxes the lower oesophageal sphincter.

supplements.name: Psyllium husk
supplements.dose: 5–10 g daily with plenty of water
supplements.mech: Soluble fibre — helps both constipation and diarrhoea, and lowers LDL.
supplements.caution: Introduce slowly with fluid; separate from medicines by two hours.

supplements.name: Digestive enzymes
supplements.mech: Bloating and incomplete digestion; pancreatic insufficiency needs prescription-strength enzymes.
supplements.caution: Not a substitute for investigating persistent symptoms.

supplements.name: Betaine HCl
supplements.mech: Hypochlorhydria contributing to bloating and poor mineral absorption.
supplements.caution: Never with active ulcer, gastritis, or on a PPI or NSAID.

supplements.name: L-glutamine
supplements.dose: 5 g one to three times daily
supplements.mech: Fuel for enterocytes; used for intestinal barrier repair.
supplements.caution: Caution in cirrhosis and in active malignancy.

supplements.name: Milk thistle (Silybum marianum)
supplements.mech: Hepatoprotective; used in hepatitis and fatty liver.
supplements.caution: Generally safe; mild laxative effect.

supplements.name: Melatonin for reflux
supplements.mech: Raises lower oesophageal sphincter tone; trial evidence as a reflux adjunct.
supplements.caution: Daytime grogginess at higher doses.

supplements.name: D-mannose
supplements.mech: Prevents E. coli adhesion in recurrent urinary tract infection.
supplements.caution: Not a treatment for established pyelonephritis.

supplements.name: Cranberry (PACs)
supplements.mech: Recurrent UTI prevention; anti-adhesion rather than antibacterial.
supplements.caution: Interacts with warfarin; sugar load in juices.

supplements.name: Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens)
supplements.mech: Benign prostatic hyperplasia symptoms.
supplements.caution: Trial results are mixed; mild antiplatelet effect.

supplements.name: Beta-sitosterol
supplements.mech: Improves urinary flow in BPH with more consistent trial support than saw palmetto.
supplements.caution: Well tolerated.

supplements.name: Lycopene
supplements.mech: Prostate health and antioxidant support.
supplements.caution: Take with fat.

supplements.name: Vitex agnus-castus (chaste tree)
supplements.mech: Luteal phase support, PMS, cyclical breast pain and irregular cycles; acts on dopamine and prolactin.
supplements.caution: Takes three cycles. Interacts with dopaminergic drugs and hormonal contraception.

supplements.name: DIM / indole-3-carbinol
supplements.mech: Supports oestrogen metabolism toward the 2-hydroxy pathway.
supplements.caution: Can cause headache and darkened urine.

supplements.name: Black cohosh (Actaea racemosa)
supplements.mech: Vasomotor symptoms of menopause.
supplements.caution: Rare hepatotoxicity — stop with any jaundice or dark urine.

supplements.name: Maca (Lepidium meyenii)
supplements.mech: Libido, energy and menopausal symptoms without direct hormonal action.
supplements.caution: Caution with thyroid disease — goitrogenic raw.

supplements.name: Glucosamine and chondroitin
supplements.mech: Osteoarthritis, especially of the knee; effect is modest and slow.
supplements.caution: Shellfish-derived forms in allergy; may affect glucose control slightly.

supplements.name: Collagen peptides
supplements.mech: Joint, skin and connective tissue support; some trial support in osteoarthritis.
supplements.caution: Take with vitamin C.

supplements.name: MSM
supplements.mech: Sulphur donor used for joint pain and inflammation.
supplements.caution: Mild GI upset.

supplements.name: Tart cherry
supplements.mech: Lowers urate and eases gout flares; also studied for sleep.
supplements.caution: Sugar load in juice form.

supplements.name: Bromelain
supplements.mech: Proteolytic anti-inflammatory for sinusitis, injury and oedema; pairs with quercetin.
supplements.caution: Antiplatelet effect; pineapple allergy.

supplements.name: Astragalus membranaceus
supplements.mech: Immune tonic for recurrent infection; used long-term rather than acutely.
supplements.caution: Traditionally avoided during an acute fever; theoretical interaction with immunosuppressants.

supplements.name: Medicinal mushrooms
supplements.mech: Beta-glucan immune modulation in recurrent infection and immune dysregulation.
supplements.caution: Choose fruiting-body extracts; caution with immunosuppressants.

supplements.name: Liquorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra)
supplements.mech: Demulcent and antiviral; adrenal support in fatigue.
supplements.caution: Whole liquorice raises blood pressure and lowers potassium — not for hypertension; use DGL for gut work.

supplements.name: Adaptogen blends
supplements.mech: HPA-axis support in fatigue and chronic stress.
supplements.caution: Stimulating adaptogens destabilise mood in bipolar disorder — check the ingredient list.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.mech: Muscle and cognitive support; emerging evidence in depression and fatigue.
supplements.caution: Take with adequate fluid.

supplements.name: L-carnitine
supplements.mech: Fatty acid transport into mitochondria; fatigue and male fertility.
supplements.caution: Fishy odour at high doses; TMAO questions.

supplements.name: D-ribose
supplements.dose: 5 g up to three times daily
supplements.mech: ATP substrate used in fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue.
supplements.caution: Can lower blood glucose.

supplements.name: Phosphatidylserine
supplements.mech: Blunts an exaggerated cortisol response; cognition.
supplements.caution: Take earlier in the day.

supplements.name: Lion's mane (Hericium erinaceus)
supplements.mech: Nerve growth factor support; cognition and mild mood benefit.
supplements.caution: Rare skin reactions.

supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
supplements.mech: Cerebral and peripheral circulation; cognition; Raynaud's.
supplements.caution: Antiplatelet effect — stop two weeks before surgery and avoid with anticoagulants.

supplements.name: Hawthorn (Crataegus)
supplements.mech: Mild heart failure and hypertension; improves exercise tolerance.
supplements.caution: Potentiates digoxin and antihypertensives.

supplements.name: Diosmin / hesperidin (citrus flavonoids)
supplements.mech: Venous tone in varicose veins, haemorrhoids and chronic venous insufficiency — the best-supported oral agent.
supplements.caution: GI upset; avoid in pregnancy.

supplements.name: Horse chestnut seed extract
supplements.mech: Chronic venous insufficiency and leg oedema.
supplements.caution: Standardised extracts only — raw seed is toxic.

supplements.name: Butcher's broom (Ruscus)
supplements.mech: Venous tone and haemorrhoids.
supplements.caution: Caution in hypertension.

supplements.name: Gotu kola (Centella asiatica)
supplements.mech: Connective tissue and venous integrity; wound healing; anxiolytic.
supplements.caution: Rare hepatotoxicity with long use.

supplements.name: Aloe vera (inner leaf)
supplements.mech: Mucosal soothing in reflux and IBD; topical for burns and wounds.
supplements.caution: Whole-leaf latex is a harsh stimulant laxative — use inner-leaf preparations orally.

supplements.name: Vitamin A
supplements.mech: Epithelial integrity, immune function, wound healing.
supplements.caution: Teratogenic — strict limits in pregnancy. Hepatotoxic long-term.

supplements.name: Vitamin E (mixed tocopherols)
supplements.mech: Antioxidant; membrane protection.
supplements.caution: Antiplatelet at higher doses; use mixed tocopherols, not alpha alone.

supplements.name: Colostrum / immunoglobulins
supplements.mech: Gut barrier and mucosal immunity.
supplements.caution: Dairy-derived — avoid in milk protein allergy.

supplements.name: Choline and inositol (lipotropics)
supplements.mech: Fat mobilisation in fatty liver and cholestasis.
supplements.caution: GI upset; fishy odour with high choline.

supplements.name: Taurine
supplements.mech: Bile conjugation, cardiac and neuronal stability.
supplements.caution: Well tolerated.

therapies.name: Mayan abdominal massage
therapies.what: Non-invasive external massage of the abdomen that repositions abdominal and pelvic organs to relieve pain, increasing blood flow, moving lymph and restoring nerve signalling. Your coursework names dysmenorrhoea, endometriosis, irritable bowel syndrome and infertility as the conditions it may help.
therapies.caution: Requires training in anatomy, physiology and the traditional technique. Avoid over an IUD without training, in pregnancy, and over acute inflammation or a known mass. Self-massage handouts make a good take-home practice.

therapies.name: Sauna and induced sweating
therapies.what: One of the safest routes of elimination — it does not load the liver or kidneys. Any sweating counts: sauna, exercise or a sweatsuit. Start at 5 minutes and build; replete minerals before and after.
therapies.caution: Shower immediately afterwards with Castile soap to prevent reabsorption. Avoid shared or smelly saunas — aerosolised toxins from other users can be absorbed.

therapies.name: Lymphatic drainage
therapies.what: Vibration plates, dry brushing, and the “Big 6” sequence — clavicles, behind the ears, axillae, stomach, back, groin and behind the knees. Done daily in the shower while soaping up.
therapies.caution: Often overlooked; open drainage before mobilising anything.

therapies.name: Binder push-pull protocol
therapies.what: The mould detox base from your lecture: AM/PM push-pull, 5 days on and 2 days off, over 4–6 months before retesting. Start at ¼ teaspoon and increase as tolerated. Keep the binder even if only one dose is taken.
therapies.caution: Do not detox during known ongoing exposure, active colonisation, severe constipation, or extreme sensitivity. Poor tolerance is a signal, not a reason to push.

therapies.name: Environmental remediation
therapies.what: Inspection with heat-signature technology by a certified inspector, separate HVAC assessment, and mould dogs where available. HEPA filtration where relocation is not possible. Check crawl spaces, cars, and items brought from a mouldy home.
therapies.caution: Standard mould inspectors are not licensed for HVAC. Belongings can carry the exposure to a new home.

therapies.name: Sinus irrigation and antimicrobial sprays
therapies.what: Colloidal silver with herbs (RNA/ACS) first line for up to 12 weeks; xylitol with grapefruit seed extract where biofilm is a factor; compounded antifungal or antibacterial sprays where needed. Reset afterwards with Lactobacillus sakei.
therapies.caution: Treat sinuses last — oral and IV routes do not reliably reach them. Your lecture rates colloidal silver above BEG spray for MARCONS on cost, tolerability and resistance.

therapies.name: CPAP / BiPAP
therapies.what: Positive airway pressure — the mainstay for obstructive sleep apnoea, and BiPAP in type 2 respiratory failure.
therapies.caution: Adherence is the whole battle: mask fit, humidification and desensitisation determine success.

therapies.name: Mandibular advancement device
therapies.what: Jaw repositioning appliance for mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnoea, or where CPAP is not tolerated.
therapies.caution: Needs a dentist experienced in sleep appliances; can shift the bite over time.

therapies.name: Positional therapy
therapies.what: Lateral decubitus sleeping improves obstructive sleep apnoea; supine makes it worse.
therapies.caution: Simple, free, and worth trying in every positional apnoea.

therapies.name: Upper airway stimulation
therapies.what: Implanted stimulation of the hypoglossal nerve to advance the tongue base during sleep.
therapies.caution: For selected CPAP-intolerant patients; the hypoglossal nerve is the structure stimulated, not the genioglossus directly.

therapies.name: Airway surgery
therapies.what: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty, tonsillectomy or adenoidectomy where anatomy is the obstruction — often the answer in children.
therapies.caution: Adult results are variable; assess anatomy before offering.

therapies.name: Supplemental oxygen
therapies.what: Long-term oxygen in severe COPD with resting hypoxaemia; acute use in respiratory failure.
therapies.caution: Nasal cannula flow starts around 1 L/min. Use the minimum effective concentration — 60–100% risks oxygen toxicity. SpO2 92% or less needs more advanced care; 88% or less needs the emergency department.

therapies.name: Pulmonary rehabilitation
therapies.what: Supervised exercise, breathing retraining and education — one of the few interventions that improves quality of life and admissions in COPD.
therapies.caution: An FEV1/FVC around 40% is too low to start unsupervised exercise; refer to a programme instead.

therapies.name: Breathing retraining
therapies.what: Buteyko, diaphragmatic and pursed-lip breathing for asthma, COPD and anxious hyperventilation.
therapies.caution: Adjunct to, not a replacement for, controller therapy.

therapies.name: Airway clearance
therapies.what: Postural drainage, percussion, oscillating PEP devices and nebulised hypertonic saline to mobilise secretions in bronchiectasis and cystic fibrosis.
therapies.caution: Daily and lifelong in bronchiectasis — the single most important measure.

therapies.name: Smoking cessation programme
therapies.what: Behavioural support with pharmacotherapy — the only intervention that changes the slope of decline in COPD.
therapies.caution: Combine counselling with NRT or varenicline; screen mood before varenicline.

therapies.name: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT)
therapies.what: First-line trauma therapy targeting distorted beliefs and “stuck points” — guilt and shame — after trauma.
therapies.caution: Psychotherapy, not medication, is first-line in PTSD.

therapies.name: Prolonged Exposure (PE)
therapies.what: Gradual, repeated imaginal and in vivo exposure to trauma cues to reduce avoidance and allow habituation.
therapies.caution: Benzodiazepines interfere with the extinction learning this depends on.

therapies.name: EMDR
therapies.what: Bilateral stimulation, such as guided eye movements, while recalling the trauma, to reprocess and integrate fragmented memories.
therapies.caution: First-line for PTSD alongside CPT and PE.

therapies.name: Cognitive behavioural therapy
therapies.what: First-line psychological treatment for depression, anxiety, insomnia (CBT-I) and chronic pain.
therapies.caution: CBT-I outperforms hypnotics for chronic insomnia and its gains last.

therapies.name: Mindfulness and yoga
therapies.what: Manages hyperarousal by engaging the parasympathetic nervous system and vagal tone, and downregulating the amygdala.
therapies.caution: Trauma-informed instruction matters — body-focused practice can be activating early in PTSD.

therapies.name: Anti-inflammatory / Mediterranean diet
therapies.what: Whole foods, vegetables and fruit, whole grains, lean protein, olive oil, avocado and fatty fish. Lowers the pro-inflammatory cytokines raised in depression and bipolar disorder.
therapies.caution: The dietary pattern with the broadest evidence across the conditions in this index.

therapies.name: Elimination diet
therapies.what: Structured removal and reintroduction to identify food triggers; your mental health notes name gluten and wheat specifically for anxiety and depression.
therapies.caution: Time-limited and supervised — indefinite restriction causes its own harm.

therapies.name: Blood sugar stabilisation
therapies.what: Removing refined sugar and eating regularly. Panic attacks arriving before meals point at blood glucose rather than at anxiety.
therapies.caution: Ask about meal timing before escalating an anxiolytic.

therapies.name: Caffeine reduction
therapies.what: Caffeine directly raises anxiety, disturbs sleep and can destabilise mood.
therapies.caution: Taper rather than stop abruptly to avoid withdrawal headache.

therapies.name: Sleep hygiene and circadian work
therapies.what: Fixed wake time, morning daylight, evening light restriction, and a wind-down routine.
therapies.caution: Fixing the wake time matters more than fixing the bedtime.

therapies.name: Pelvic floor therapy
therapies.what: Relaxes and strengthens the muscles and ligaments of the pelvic floor in men and women to reduce pain and the symptoms that follow conditions such as the postpartum period. Your reflection names urinary incontinence and frequency in male patients, endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain in female patients, and constipation among the digestive complaints it helps. Supervised training beats unguided Kegels.
therapies.caution: An overactive pelvic floor needs downtraining, not strengthening; assess before prescribing exercises.

therapies.name: Diaphragmatic breathing
therapies.what: Breathing with awareness of how the belly moves on the inhale and exhale. It reduces stress, builds awareness around breathing, and improves circulation to the abdomen and pelvis. To teach it: have the patient find a quiet place, sit or lie down, and rest one hand on the chest and one on the abdomen; a slow deep breath in as the belly inflates, then a slow exhale as the belly relaxes and flattens.
therapies.caution: The foundation of pelvic floor work — an overactive floor will not release while the breath is held high in the chest.

therapies.name: Structured exercise
therapies.what: Aerobic and resistance work — first-line or co-equal in depression, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, osteoporosis, chronic pain and fatigue.
therapies.caution: Start below capacity in post-exertional malaise; graded exercise can harm in ME/CFS.

therapies.name: Weight management
therapies.what: The most effective single measure in obstructive sleep apnoea, type 2 diabetes, knee osteoarthritis and fatty liver.
therapies.caution: Obesity is the most common risk factor for obstructive sleep apnoea.

therapies.name: Physical therapy and manual medicine
therapies.what: Graded loading, manipulation and mobilisation for back, neck and joint pain.
therapies.caution: Imaging first only where red flags are present.

therapies.name: Constitutional hydrotherapy
therapies.what: Alternating hot and cold applications to modulate circulation, immune function and vagal tone.
therapies.caution: Avoid extremes in cardiovascular instability and neuropathy.

therapies.name: Acupuncture
therapies.what: Evidence in chronic pain, migraine prophylaxis, chemotherapy-induced nausea and hot flushes.
therapies.caution: Choose a practitioner using single-use needles and clean technique.

therapies.name: Light therapy
therapies.what: 10,000 lux for 20–30 minutes on waking in seasonal and non-seasonal depression and circadian disorder.
therapies.caution: Can trigger mania in bipolar disorder — introduce carefully and monitor.

therapies.name: Saline nasal irrigation
therapies.what: High-volume, low-pressure rinsing for sinusitis and allergic rhinitis — one of the highest-yield simple measures.
therapies.caution: Distilled or previously boiled water only, never straight from the tap.

therapies.name: Steam inhalation and humidification
therapies.what: Loosens secretions and eases upper airway irritation.
therapies.caution: Scald risk, especially with children.

therapies.name: Compression therapy
therapies.what: Graduated compression stockings for varicose veins, venous insufficiency and oedema.
therapies.caution: Check the ankle-brachial index before compressing a limb with suspected arterial disease.

therapies.name: Sitz baths and topical care
therapies.what: Warm sitz baths for haemorrhoids, fissure and post-partum perineal pain.
therapies.caution: Pat dry; avoid prolonged soaking.

therapies.name: Barrier skin care
therapies.what: Emollients, lukewarm short showers, soap substitutes — the base every eczema regimen is built on.
therapies.caution: Apply within minutes of bathing to trap moisture.

therapies.name: Wet wrap therapy
therapies.what: Damp occlusive layers over emollient or topical steroid for severe eczema flares.
therapies.caution: Short courses under guidance.

therapies.name: Narrowband UVB phototherapy
therapies.what: Moderate to severe psoriasis and refractory eczema.
therapies.caution: Cumulative dose and skin cancer risk are tracked.

therapies.name: Counselling and psychosocial support
therapies.what: Adjustment disorder, grief, chronic illness adaptation, and the psychosocial layer of every chronic condition.
therapies.caution: Adjustment disorder resolves within six months of the stressor ending — that timeline is the diagnosis.

therapies.name: Peer and group support
therapies.what: Chronic illness, addiction and caregiver burden.
therapies.caution: Complements rather than replaces individual care.

therapies.name: Vagal tone work
therapies.what: Slow paced breathing, humming, cold exposure and heart rate variability training.
therapies.caution: The mechanism behind much of the benefit of yoga and mindfulness in hyperarousal.

labs.name: CBC with differential
labs.why: The first-line screen in fatigue, infection, bleeding and before most drug therapy.
labs.interpret: Microcytic anaemia points at iron deficiency or thalassaemia; macrocytic at B12, folate, alcohol or hypothyroidism. Neutrophilia suggests bacterial infection, lymphocytosis viral, eosinophilia atopy or parasites.

labs.name: Comprehensive metabolic panel
labs.why: Electrolytes, glucose, renal and liver function — baseline before and during most drug therapy.
labs.interpret: Hyponatraemia raises Legionella, SIADH and paraneoplastic syndromes. A reversed albumin/globulin ratio appears in sarcoidosis.

labs.name: TSH with free T4
labs.why: Any fatigue, weight change, mood change, menstrual disturbance, constipation or hair loss — and mandatory before attributing psychiatric symptoms to a primary psychiatric cause.
labs.interpret: High TSH with low free T4 is primary hypothyroidism; suppressed TSH with high free T4 is hyperthyroidism.

labs.name: Thyroid antibodies (TPO, TG)
labs.why: Distinguishing autoimmune thyroid disease from other causes.
labs.interpret: Positive TPO indicates Hashimoto's or Graves' autoimmunity.

labs.name: Free T3 and reverse T3
labs.why: Conversion problems and persistent symptoms on adequate levothyroxine.
labs.interpret: High reverse T3 with low free T3 suggests impaired conversion under stress or illness.

labs.name: Ferritin with iron studies
labs.why: Fatigue, hair loss, restless legs, heavy periods, and before iron supplementation.
labs.interpret: Ferritin under 30 ng/mL is deficiency even with a normal haemoglobin; it is an acute-phase reactant, so read it alongside CRP. Under 50 is often symptomatic in restless legs and hair loss.

labs.name: B12, folate and methylmalonic acid
labs.why: Fatigue, neuropathy, cognitive change, macrocytosis, and anyone on metformin or a long-term PPI.
labs.interpret: Methylmalonic acid confirms functional B12 deficiency when serum B12 sits in the low-normal grey zone.

labs.name: 25-hydroxyvitamin D
labs.why: Fatigue, mood, bone health, autoimmune and respiratory conditions; sleep apnoea severity tracks with deficiency.
labs.interpret: 25-hydroxy is the storage form to measure. Elevated 1,25-dihydroxy in someone not supplementing suggests granulomatous disease such as sarcoidosis.

labs.name: Lipid panel
labs.why: Cardiovascular risk assessment.
labs.interpret: Cholesterol that will not respond to diet and lifestyle may have an environmental toxicant component — one of the flags in your mould lecture.

labs.name: HbA1c
labs.why: Diagnosis and monitoring of type 2 diabetes; screening in obesity, PCOS and metabolic syndrome.
labs.interpret: 5.7–6.4% is prediabetes, 6.5% or above is diabetes. Falsely low with shortened red cell survival.

labs.name: Fasting insulin and glucose (HOMA-IR)
labs.why: Insulin resistance before HbA1c moves — PCOS, metabolic syndrome, fatty liver.
labs.interpret: Raised fasting insulin with normal glucose is early insulin resistance.

labs.name: hs-CRP and ESR
labs.why: Inflammatory burden; monitoring autoimmune and infectious disease.
labs.interpret: Very high ESR with headache and jaw claudication in an older patient means giant cell arteritis until excluded.

labs.name: Procalcitonin
labs.why: Separating bacterial from viral lower respiratory infection and guiding antibiotic decisions.
labs.interpret: Rises in typical bacterial pneumonia; stays low in viral pneumonia and in the atypicals — Legionella, Chlamydia, Mycoplasma and Bordetella.

labs.name: D-dimer
labs.why: The first diagnostic step in suspected pulmonary embolism of LOW clinical likelihood.
labs.interpret: A negative result in a low-probability patient excludes PE. It is non-specific — a positive result needs CT angiography.

labs.name: Arterial blood gases
labs.why: Respiratory failure, severe exacerbation, and assessing ventilation.
labs.interpret: Type 1 failure is low oxygen with normal or low CO2; type 2 adds CO2 retention. PE classically gives low O2 with low CO2 from hyperventilation.

labs.name: BNP / NT-proBNP
labs.why: Separating cardiac from pulmonary causes of breathlessness; heart failure diagnosis and monitoring.
labs.interpret: A normal value makes untreated heart failure unlikely.

labs.name: Troponin
labs.why: Suspected acute coronary syndrome.
labs.interpret: Serial measurement; any rise with chest pain is an emergency.

labs.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin
labs.why: COPD in a young patient, a non-smoker, or with a family history.
labs.interpret: Low levels allow unopposed elastase to destroy elastin — the mechanism of early emphysema.

labs.name: Total and specific IgE, or skin prick testing
labs.why: Identifying allergic triggers in asthma, rhinitis and eczema.
labs.interpret: Guides both avoidance and biologic selection in severe asthma.

labs.name: Blood eosinophil count
labs.why: Phenotyping asthma and COPD — it decides who benefits from an inhaled corticosteroid or an anti-IL5 biologic.
labs.interpret: Read from the CBC differential.

labs.name: ANA with extractable antigens
labs.why: Screening for systemic autoimmune disease when there are multi-system features.
labs.interpret: A positive ANA alone is common and non-diagnostic; the pattern, titre and specific antibodies carry the meaning.

labs.name: Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP
labs.why: Suspected rheumatoid arthritis.
labs.interpret: Anti-CCP is the more specific and predicts erosive disease.

labs.name: Serum urate
labs.why: Gout diagnosis and urate-lowering targets.
labs.interpret: Can be normal during an acute flare — recheck two weeks later. Target under 6 mg/dL, or under 5 with tophi.

labs.name: Creatine kinase
labs.why: Muscle pain on a statin, and myopathy.
labs.interpret: Marked elevation with weakness needs the statin stopped.

labs.name: Liver enzymes and bilirubin
labs.why: Hepatitis, fatty liver, and monitoring hepatotoxic drugs and botanicals.
labs.interpret: An ALT above AST suggests fatty liver; AST above ALT in a 2:1 ratio suggests alcohol.

labs.name: Viral hepatitis serology
labs.why: Suspected or confirmed hepatitis; before immunosuppression.
labs.interpret: Hepatitis B must be excluded before starting a biologic.

labs.name: H. pylori testing
labs.why: Dyspepsia, gastritis and ulcer.
labs.interpret: Urea breath test or stool antigen; stop PPIs two weeks and antibiotics four weeks before testing or it will read falsely negative.

labs.name: Coeliac serology (tTG-IgA with total IgA)
labs.why: Iron deficiency, diarrhoea, bloating, unexplained weight loss and fatigue.
labs.interpret: Must be done while still eating gluten. Total IgA is needed to interpret a negative result.

labs.name: Stool culture, ova and parasites, PCR panel
labs.why: Persistent or bloody diarrhoea, travel history, and suspected parasites.
labs.interpret: A PCR panel is more sensitive than microscopy; treat on a positive result rather than on suspicion.

labs.name: Faecal calprotectin
labs.why: Separating inflammatory bowel disease from irritable bowel syndrome.
labs.interpret: A normal value makes IBD unlikely and can spare a colonoscopy.

labs.name: Faecal occult blood / FIT
labs.why: Colorectal cancer screening; blood on the rectal glove.
labs.interpret: A positive result needs colonoscopy, not repeat testing.

labs.name: Comprehensive stool analysis
labs.why: Dysbiosis, digestive capacity and inflammation in functional GI presentations.
labs.interpret: Interpret alongside symptoms; findings are frequently over-read.

labs.name: SIBO breath test
labs.why: Bloating, distension and IBS with a suspected overgrowth.
labs.interpret: Hydrogen and methane over the test period; methane-positive patients tend toward constipation.

labs.name: Urinalysis with microscopy
labs.why: Urinary symptoms, flank pain, and as part of any systemic workup.
labs.interpret: Nitrites and leukocyte esterase point at infection; microhaematuria appears in stones, Legionella and glomerular disease.

labs.name: Urine culture and sensitivity
labs.why: Recurrent, complicated or treatment-failing urinary infection.
labs.interpret: Take before starting antibiotics wherever possible.

labs.name: Legionella and pneumococcal urinary antigen
labs.why: Pneumonia with GI symptoms, hyponatraemia, or exposure to water systems, cooling towers or swamp coolers.
labs.interpret: The urinary antigen test is what confirms Legionella — the exposure history is the clue that prompts it.

labs.name: PSA
labs.why: Prostate assessment alongside the digital rectal exam, after a shared decision about screening.
labs.interpret: A 5-alpha reductase inhibitor halves the value — double it when interpreting. Prostatitis, recent ejaculation and cycling all raise it.

labs.name: STI testing (NAAT)
labs.why: Urethral or cervical discharge, cervical motion tenderness, and new or multiple partners.
labs.interpret: Gonorrhoea and chlamydia by NAAT; add trichomonas, syphilis serology and HIV as indicated.

labs.name: Vaginal wet mount and pH
labs.why: Discharge, itch and odour.
labs.interpret: Clue cells for bacterial vaginosis, pseudohyphae for candida, motile organisms for trichomonas.

labs.name: Female hormone panel
labs.why: Irregular cycles, infertility, PCOS and menopause. Timed to the cycle — day 3 for FSH, LH and oestradiol, day 21 for progesterone.
labs.interpret: An LH:FSH ratio above 2:1 with raised free testosterone supports PCOS. FSH over 25 with amenorrhoea suggests menopause.

labs.name: Androgen panel
labs.why: Hirsutism, acne, alopecia and suspected PCOS.
labs.interpret: Free testosterone, DHEA-S and 17-OH progesterone to exclude late-onset congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

labs.name: Prolactin
labs.why: Amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea and infertility.
labs.interpret: Raised levels need a repeat, a medication review, and imaging if persistent.

labs.name: Cortisol rhythm (salivary or dried urine)
labs.why: Fatigue, stress-related presentations and suspected HPA dysregulation.
labs.interpret: Four-point sampling shows the curve rather than a single value. In PTSD your notes describe high CRH with blunted ACTH and low cortisol.

labs.name: Semen analysis
labs.why: Male factor in infertility — the first test, before extensive female workup.
labs.interpret: Repeat after 6–12 weeks before drawing conclusions.

labs.name: DEXA bone density
labs.why: Osteoporosis screening and monitoring.
labs.interpret: T-score at or below −2.5 is osteoporosis; −1.0 to −2.5 is osteopenia.

labs.name: Chest X-ray
labs.why: Cough over three weeks, suspected pneumonia, breathlessness, chest trauma, and any abnormal chest exam.
labs.interpret: Lobar infiltrate confirms pneumonia. In asthma it shows hyperinflation, increased markings and atelectasis in children — patchy infiltration is not typical. It cannot confirm COPD.

labs.name: Chest CT
labs.why: Interstitial disease, bronchiectasis, nodules, and characterising anything unclear on plain film.
labs.interpret: Tram-track, signet-ring and honeycomb signs appear in bronchiectasis and fibrosis; non-caseating granulomas are a histological finding, not a radiological one.

labs.name: CT pulmonary angiography
labs.why: The imaging study that rules out pulmonary embolism.
labs.interpret: The definitive test; V/Q scanning is the alternative where contrast or radiation is a problem.

labs.name: Spirometry with bronchodilator response
labs.why: Diagnosing and staging asthma and COPD — spirometry alone confirms COPD, without CT or plain film.
labs.interpret: An FEV1/FVC ratio at or below 70% indicates obstruction. FEV1 falls with methacholine and rises with albuterol in asthma. Long-standing asthma raises FRC, RV and TLC, but not vital capacity.

labs.name: Peak flow monitoring
labs.why: Home monitoring of asthma control and treatment response — not a diagnostic test.
labs.interpret: Track against the patient's own personal best, not a population value.

labs.name: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO)
labs.why: Type 2 airway inflammation; predicting steroid response in asthma.
labs.interpret: Falls with adherence to inhaled steroids — useful for checking it.

labs.name: Polysomnography
labs.why: The gold standard for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnoea, after a positive screening questionnaire.
labs.interpret: The Apnea-Hypopnea Index from this study determines severity — not neck circumference or the questionnaire score.

labs.name: STOP-BANG questionnaire
labs.why: The first step in suspected sleep apnoea — a clinically relevant score is what supports going on to polysomnography.
labs.interpret: Snoring, Tiredness, Observed apnoea, Pressure, BMI, Age, Neck, Gender.

labs.name: Epworth Sleepiness Scale
labs.why: Quantifying daytime sleepiness and tracking response to treatment.
labs.interpret: Measures sleepiness, not apnoea — it does not gate polysomnography.

labs.name: Sputum Gram stain and culture
labs.why: Pneumonia not responding as expected, and suspected resistant or unusual organisms.
labs.interpret: Red currant-jelly sputum suggests Klebsiella. A foul taste with dullness and absent breath sounds suggests lung abscess.

labs.name: Sputum acid-fast bacilli and TB NAAT
labs.why: Chronic cough with haemoptysis, night sweats, weight loss or travel to an endemic area.
labs.interpret: Microscopy showing acid-fast bacilli is not definitive by itself — culture confirms. A Mantoux reading of 5 mm is positive only in defined high-risk groups.

labs.name: Sweat chloride (pilocarpine iontophoresis)
labs.why: Cystic fibrosis — recurrent bronchitis, sinus disease, steatorrhoea and failure to thrive in a child.
labs.interpret: Elevated sweat sodium, chloride or potassium confirms the diagnosis.

labs.name: Thoracentesis with fluid analysis
labs.why: Characterising a pleural effusion.
labs.interpret: Transudate points at left-sided heart failure, hypoalbuminaemia or cirrhosis; exudate at pneumonia, malignancy, tuberculosis or embolism.

labs.name: Right heart catheterisation
labs.why: The gold standard confirming pulmonary artery hypertension.
labs.interpret: Required before any pulmonary vasodilator — sarcoidosis in particular should not be treated empirically with prostacyclin derivatives.

labs.name: Echocardiogram
labs.why: Murmurs, heart failure, and screening for pulmonary hypertension before catheterisation.
labs.interpret: Gives ejection fraction, valve function and estimated pulmonary pressures.

labs.name: 12-lead EKG
labs.why: Chest pain, palpitations, syncope, an irregular pulse, and before starting QT-prolonging drugs.
labs.interpret: Read in a fixed order: rate, rhythm, QRS, P waves, PR interval, ST segments, delta waves, T waves — the eight-step sequence from your EKG assignment.

labs.name: Ambulatory EKG monitoring
labs.why: Intermittent palpitations, syncope and suspected paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
labs.interpret: Longer recording raises the yield when symptoms are infrequent.

labs.name: Ankle-brachial index
labs.why: Claudication, absent pulses, non-healing leg ulcer — and before compressing any limb.
labs.interpret: At or below 0.9 indicates peripheral arterial disease; above 1.3 suggests non-compressible calcified vessels.

labs.name: Venous duplex ultrasound
labs.why: Suspected deep vein thrombosis, varicose veins and venous insufficiency.
labs.interpret: The first-line test for a swollen, tender calf.

labs.name: Carotid ultrasound
labs.why: Carotid bruit, transient ischaemic attack or stroke.
labs.interpret: Quantifies stenosis and guides intervention.

labs.name: Abdominal aortic ultrasound
labs.why: A widened or expansile aortic pulsation, and one-time screening in older men who have smoked.
labs.interpret: Diameter over 3 cm defines an aneurysm.

labs.name: Abdominal ultrasound
labs.why: Right upper quadrant pain, abnormal liver enzymes, suspected gallstones, hepatomegaly and fatty liver.
labs.interpret: First-line for gallstones and for characterising the liver.

labs.name: Renal and bladder ultrasound
labs.why: Stones, obstruction, recurrent infection and post-void residual.
labs.interpret: Avoids radiation; CT is more sensitive for small stones.

labs.name: CT abdomen and pelvis
labs.why: Acute abdomen, suspected appendicitis, renal colic and unexplained mass.
labs.interpret: Non-contrast CT is the standard for renal colic.

labs.name: Pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal)
labs.why: Pelvic pain, abnormal bleeding, adnexal mass, fibroids and PCOS morphology.
labs.interpret: Polycystic morphology supports but does not by itself make the PCOS diagnosis.

labs.name: Mammography and breast ultrasound
labs.why: A breast lump, skin or nipple change, and routine screening.
labs.interpret: Any discrete new lump needs imaging regardless of a reassuring examination.

labs.name: Colonoscopy
labs.why: Rectal bleeding, a rectal mass, altered bowel habit over 50, a positive FIT, and IBD assessment.
labs.interpret: The investigation a palpable rectal mass or blood on the glove leads to.

labs.name: Upper endoscopy
labs.why: Alarm dyspepsia — weight loss, dysphagia, anaemia, vomiting, or onset over 50 — and reflux not responding to therapy.
labs.interpret: Allows biopsy for H. pylori, coeliac disease and Barrett's oesophagus.

labs.name: MRI spine
labs.why: Back pain with neurological deficit, suspected cauda equina, or red flags for infection or malignancy.
labs.interpret: Cauda equina syndrome is an emergency MRI, not a routine request.

labs.name: Plain radiograph of a joint
labs.why: Trauma, deformity and osteoarthritis assessment.
labs.interpret: Radiographic change and symptom severity correlate poorly in osteoarthritis.

labs.name: MRI of a joint
labs.why: Suspected ligament or meniscal tear, and persistent pain with a normal radiograph.
labs.interpret: Order when the result would change management.

labs.name: Joint aspiration with crystal analysis and culture
labs.why: A hot, swollen, acutely tender joint — the test that separates gout from septic arthritis.
labs.interpret: Negatively birefringent needle crystals mean gout; a positive Gram stain or culture means septic arthritis and admission.

labs.name: Skin biopsy
labs.why: Undiagnosed rash, suspicious pigmented lesion, and a non-healing ulcer.
labs.interpret: The answer for anything atypical or refractory.

labs.name: KOH preparation and fungal culture
labs.why: Suspected tinea, candida and onychomycosis.
labs.interpret: Confirm before committing to months of oral antifungal therapy.

labs.name: Urine mycotoxin panel
labs.why: Suspected mould illness — the multi-system picture your lecture describes.
labs.interpret: Vibrant Wellness covers 29 mycotoxins plus total burden and also runs metals and environmental toxicants; Mosaic covers 11; Real Time 16. Pick one company and stay with it so results stay comparable.

labs.name: Organic Acids Test (OAT)
labs.why: Fungal colonisation, mitochondrial and neurotransmitter markers.
labs.interpret: Detects Aspergillus and Fusarium colonisation. The arabinose marker suggests candida; high oxalic acid suggests fungal colonisation and can mimic fibromyalgia.

labs.name: Shoemaker inflammatory markers
labs.why: Selected mould workup where the result will change the plan.
labs.interpret: TGF-beta-1 for inflammation and possible current exposure; C4a as a mould exposure marker; C3a for bacterial and Lyme reactivation. Only order labs that give actionable data.

labs.name: HLA-DQ genotyping
labs.why: Genetic susceptibility to mould illness.
labs.interpret: Identifies patients more sensitive to re-exposure — who may, your lecture notes, actually detect it faster. Interpretation calculators are available online.

labs.name: Nasal swab — bacterial and fungal
labs.why: Sinus colonisation, especially in treatment-resistant cases.
labs.interpret: Always order BOTH components. The fungal side is often the more important and is the one commonly missed.

labs.name: Candida antibodies (IgA, IgG, IgM)
labs.why: Suspected candida overgrowth alongside mould work.
labs.interpret: Interpret with the OAT arabinose marker and clinical picture.

labs.name: Home environmental testing
labs.why: Establishing whether the building is the source before any detox is attempted.
labs.interpret: Self-test swab kits from Real Time Labs and Micrometrics; interpret with the HERTSMI calculator. A certified inspector should use heat-signature technology, and HVAC needs its own specialist.

labs.name: Heavy metals and environmental toxicants
labs.why: Chronic multi-system illness, unexplained neurological symptoms and infertility.
